beats.narration_text: The answer is unique because it satisfies four axioms. Efficiency: credits sum to the full prediction. Symmetry: identical features get identical credit. Dummy: unused features get zero. Additivity: credits from separate models combine cleanly. No other attribution rule satisfies all four.

beats.narration_text: A recommendation model pushes article probability from 45 to 68 percent — 23 points from three signals: reading time, scroll depth, and headline clicks. A naive attribution adds reading time first and credits it 0.17. But add it last and it gets 0.09 — the value shifts with the order. Shapley averages all six orderings. Reading time's fair share: 0.14. Scroll depth: 0.06. Clicks: 0.03. They sum exactly to 0.23. That sum is guaranteed — it is the efficiency axiom working.
